proposed_from.topic: Closed-form sharp multi-regime effect bounds for a two-source binary collider SCM. Let X,Z,Y be binary in the recursive graph X→Y←Z with two mutually independent latent roots shared along X↔Y and Z↔Y and independent private outcome noise. Given normalized strictly positive tables A(x,y)=P(X=x,Y=y | do(Z=0)) and B(z,y)=P(Z=z,Y=y | do(X=0)), set p=A(0,0)+A(0,1), r=B(0,0)+B(0,1), a=A(0,1), and b=B(0,1). Prove compatibility iff -(1-p)r≤a-b≤p(1-r), and prove that q=P(Y=1 | do(X=0,Z=0)) has the sharp interval [max{a,b,a+b-pr}, min{a+1-p,b+1-r,a+b+(1-p)(1-r)}]. Construct source-preserving finite SCMs attaining every real interval point and rational endpoint certificates for rational inputs. Give the constant-time compatibility/endpoint procedure and an optional simultaneous-multinomial outer confidence interval, while excluding any general thicket compiler or field-tier claim. Credit Duarte et al., JASA 2024, Autobounds as the same-input generic polynomial-program comparator and Zaffalon et al., IJAR 2023, as adjacent multi-source approximate bounding work; Autobounds is the software consumer whose generic optimization would be replaced by this analytic certificate. PRESOLVE EVIDENCE REQUIRING VERIFICATION: Independent derivation parameterized the fiber by c and d, obtaining q=a+b-c+d, and built one finite private-threshold law matching all eight table cells. Exact checks matched 1,225 positive denominator-eight table pairs to LP values, including 42 pinned-c cases, and reconstructed 3,339 finite SCMs; the positive witness yields [1/8,1/2], and a correlated-source control escapes the valid independent-source bound. Current primary-source searches found generic methods but no exact formula collision. UNRESOLVED BOTTLENECK: Independently verify the universal source-preserving threshold extension in Section 4: one finite private-noise law and one deterministic outcome function must reproduce every prescribed response and both complete experimental tables. EARLY KILL TEST: Reconstruct both endpoint SCMs for A=((1/8,3/8),(3/8,1/8)) and B=((3/8,1/8),(3/8,1/8)); require exact agreement with all eight cells, mutually independent roots, and target values 3/8 and 5/8. seed_details.title: Closed-form compatibility and an attained risk interval for two collider experiments
seed_details.anchor_location: Sections 3--4, Theorem 1, and Section 9 of the arXiv version were checked; the theorem turns discrete causal bounds into sharp polynomial programs and the conclusion identifies analytic simplification as an open direction.
seed_details.opportunity: Eliminate the same-input polynomial program for the fixed binary collider into one compatibility inequality and two three-branch endpoint formulas, with one source-preserving SCM for every feasible target value.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace canonical response-function enumeration by a four-stratum mass reduction that retains the product law of the two latent roots.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches for the exact joint-intervention target, the expression \(a+b-pr\), and binary-collider bounds with independent latent roots returned generic bounding papers and collider-bias papers, but no formula collision.
seed_details.red_team: Immediate from Duarte et al. because their sharp polynomial program already handles arbitrary discrete experiments.
seed_details.rebuttal: Their theorem certifies a generic optimization problem; it does not state this compatibility frontier, its closed-form projection, or a common small SCM certificate for every point.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: The seed uses the SCM-native M20 shape, names the analytic fiber and certificate procedure, and does not present generic finite canonicalization as new.

seed_details.title: The simultaneous region of all four joint-intervention risks
seed_details.anchor_location: Section 3.2 constructs one shared Boolean response-function law and projects it to overlapping marginal SCMs; Section 5 notes the doubly exponential growth beyond two causes.
seed_details.opportunity: Describe the joint image of all four probabilities \(P(Y=1\mid\operatorname{do}(X=x,Z=z))\), rather than optimizing four coordinates separately.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace scalar elimination in the two-coordinate fiber by simultaneous projection into four target coordinates while retaining one deterministic outcome map.
seed_details.destination_search: The target--method search found Gresele et al.'s projection framework, Duarte et al.'s scalar optimization, and Sachs et al.'s symbolic linear programs, but no joint-image description for this independent-source menu.
seed_details.red_team: Immediate by running a generic optimizer in many directions and intersecting the resulting half-spaces.
seed_details.rebuttal: Finite directional runs do not certify the full image, its facets, or attainment by one source-preserving law; nonlinear cross-coordinate restrictions may remain.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: The object is the complete graphical response region, not four repackaged marginal intervals.

seed_details.title: Compatibility and all-zero risk bounds for a three-parent collider
seed_details.anchor_location: The abstract, reduced multilinear-program construction, and conclusion were checked; the objective degree falls with the number of intervened districts, but the method does not give this source-overlap formula.
seed_details.opportunity: Derive an explicit compatibility system and an attained all-zero joint-intervention interval from three single-parent experimental tables.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace two-way interval intersection by elimination on an eight-cell product-source response object.
seed_details.destination_search: The search found generic canonical SCM programs, hyperarc pruning, and approximate multi-study fusion, but no exact three-parent source-specific collider characterization.
seed_details.red_team: A routine induction on the number of parents extends the two-source rectangle.
seed_details.rebuttal: The third source introduces higher-order product constraints that pairwise compatibility cannot detect, so the first elimination step is not inductive.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: The seed names the new higher-order compatibility object and does not promise a general thicket compiler.

seed_details.title: Support-stratified collider bounds with structural zeros
seed_details.anchor_location: Theorem 1 and Appendix A were checked; canonical partitions preserve all categorical counterfactual distributions, but do not classify boundary support faces analytically.
seed_details.opportunity: Catalogue compatibility and attained target intervals on every support mask of the two regime tables.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace division by positive stratum masses with support-mask-specific active-face elimination.
seed_details.destination_search: The destination search found canonical finite reductions and small latent-variable feasibility methods, but no support catalogue for this two-regime collider.
seed_details.red_team: The positive formulas extend by continuity after assigning arbitrary responses on zero-mass strata.
seed_details.rebuttal: Continuity gives outer limits but does not decide which equalities delete response types or whether each boundary endpoint is attained on the same support face.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: The seed asks for an iff support catalogue and endpoint witnesses, not a boundary plug-in heuristic.

seed_details.title: A critical dependence budget for escape from independent-source bounds
seed_details.anchor_location: Sections 3--4 explicitly polynomialize products of independent disturbance probabilities; this is the first algebraic step altered by a dependence budget.
seed_details.opportunity: Index compatibility and the risk interval by a total-variation or information budget on the joint latent law, and derive the smallest budget at which the independent interval is breached.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace latent-cell factorization by a constrained coupling problem and derive its critical budget.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches found inflation and generic constrained polynomial programs, but no budget-indexed formula for this experimental menu.
seed_details.red_team: This is merely a standard sensitivity analysis over a copula class.
seed_details.rebuttal: The proposed critical budget must jointly characterize data compatibility and endpoint escape while preserving both experimental tables, which is not supplied by a generic copula envelope.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: The seed includes a named critical budget and exact endpoint path, avoiding sufficient-only sensitivity.

seed_details.title: Uniform inference at compatibility boundaries and endpoint ties
seed_details.anchor_location: Section 6 and Appendix C construct confidence regions for empirical probabilities and project them through the program; the paper reports conservative regions rather than tie-specific exact asymptotics.
seed_details.opportunity: Derive a local asymptotic law and uniformly valid confidence set for the entire interval when active max/min branches change.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace projection of a generic multinomial region by a directional derivative of the explicit max/min map and a contact-set calibration.
seed_details.destination_search: The target--method search found directional-bootstrap and moment-inequality tools, but no tie-inclusive result for this collider compatibility cone.
seed_details.red_team: Fang and Santos already give the bootstrap for maxima and minima.
seed_details.rebuttal: Their generic derivative theory does not by itself handle a possibly empty estimated fiber, simultaneous lower-and-upper coverage, and local approach to this feasibility boundary.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: This is a limit-law kernel attached to a graphical bound, not a bare inference rung.

seed_details.title: The exact private-noise support complexity of collider certificates
seed_details.anchor_location: Theorem 1 and Appendix A give a general finite cardinality bound through canonical partitions; they do not minimize private support for a fixed observed menu.
seed_details.opportunity: Characterize the smallest support of private outcome noise needed to certify each rational endpoint and identify inputs attaining the worst case.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace generic canonical cardinality with a minimum common randomization of the finitely many required response probabilities.
seed_details.destination_search: The search found canonical upper bounds and Carathéodory reductions, but no menu-specific minimum-support theorem for this graph.
seed_details.red_team: Sorting the response probabilities immediately gives the minimum number of threshold atoms.
seed_details.rebuttal: Sorting supplies an upper bound; minimality permits non-threshold deterministic response patterns and requires a matching lower bound over a nondegenerate set of inputs.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: The seed asks for an iff minimum and a worst-case region, not a single small witness.

seed_details.title: Sharp collider fusion under bounded cross-study population drift
seed_details.anchor_location: Section 5 merges observational and interventional datasets with an index variable, explicitly discussing study-specific exogenous chances; Section 7 states that EMCC returns approximate inner ranges.
seed_details.opportunity: Bound the target when the two experiments need not share one latent law but their source distributions differ by a quantified budget.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace exact equality of the two regime-specific root laws by an extremal transport coupling across study populations.
seed_details.destination_search: The search found approximate indexed-study fusion and general transport sensitivity, but no closed-form sharp interval for this collider menu.
seed_details.red_team: Allowing population drift destroys the meaning of the shared joint-intervention target.
seed_details.rebuttal: A target-population law and explicit transport budget restore a well-defined target, but specifying that law adds substantial primitives absent from the present brief.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: The seed is mathematically distinct but was dropped because the additional target-population primitives would change the posed object.
